text:
kevin: FYI customer AcornApps on Private VPC (eu-west-1 <-> us-east-1) reporting intermittent 502s + high latency to Redwood API since ~03:00UTC. They say responses differ by region and occasionally see TLS errors. Can someone triage?

maya: on it. do we have the dig/curl logs from the customer?

kevin: pasted what they sent:

---
# from eu-west-1 (works mostly)
$ dig +short api.internal.acornapps
10.12.34.56

# from us-east-1 (sometimes fails)
$ dig +short api.internal.acornapps
10.98.76.54

# curl to failing ip
$ curl -vk https://api.internal.acornapps/health --resolve api.internal.acornapps:443:10.98.76.54
* Connected to 10.98.76.54 (10.98.76.54) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS alert, fatal (552): unknown CA
* SSL: certificate subjectAltName mismatch
* Closing connection 0
---

kevin: they also reported long tail latency spikes (500-800ms) around the same time window.

steven: first guess: split DNS / stale delegation or split-horizon with inconsistent A records across peered regions. second possibility: egress allowlist/firewall in their VPC blocking outbound to our cert issuer or OCSP endpoints so certs fail to validate for some worker pools. can ops-bot check for blocked egress for that account?

ops-bot: Blocked egress event detected: vpc-acorn-123 (eu-west-1) -> 52.91.72.11:443 (Let'sEncrypt OCSP) at 2026-11-01T03:05:12Z. Rule: outbound-https-deny-9834.

ivy? ivana: typo — ivana: nice catch. if OCSP/provisioning requests are blocked in eu, some workers might be serving stale certs or failing renegotiation which would explain subjectAltName/issuer errors. also TTL drift can cause clients in different AZs to hit different backends.

maya: can we get the customer to run a few repro cmds and paste outputs? ask for both dig + curl and an openssl s_client. suggested text to send:

```
# from eu instance and us instance (run both)
dig +short api.internal.acornapps
curl -vk --resolve api.internal.acornapps:443:<ip> https://api.internal.acornapps/health
openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.internal.acornapps -showcerts
traceroute -n <ip>
```

maya: also ask them to check their NAT/eip egress IPs — if egress IPs differ by region they may have allowlist asymmetry.

kevin: sent repro request to customer. they returned the openssl output for 10.98.76.54 (us-east):

---
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Let's Encrypt, CN = R3
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
139749662312000:error:0A000126:SSL routines:OPENSSL_internal:INVALID_CLIENT_HELLO:ssl/statem/statem_lib.c:---
---

steven: that verify error lines up with blocked OCSP/issuer egress OR missing CA bundle on the worker. but ops-bot already flagged blocked OCSP for eu vpc — we need to check whether the worker pool IPs in us-east are trying to validate via eu-based OCSP responders and getting different paths.

ivana: opening infra ticket INFRA-4021 to check DNS propagation and cert issuer egress routes for the account and associated worker pools. I'll include correlation with our edge pools in eu-west-1 / us-east-1 and cert rotation logs.

steven: short-term mitigation for customer: 1) add our cert issuer/OCSP IP ranges (52.91.72.0/24 and 34.201.23.0/24 — example) to their egress allowlist for both regions, 2) flush DNS caches and lower TTL while we verify, 3) if they can't change firewall immediately, they can pin their app to the eu endpoint via hosts override as temporary workaround.

maya: also recommend they add our healthcheck endpoint to their allowlist so probes aren't blocked.

kevin: customer applied an allowlist change for the OCSP IPs in eu-west and reported reduced TLS failures after ~10 minutes, but still seeing occasional 502s. I asked them to capture traceroute + our edge logs for the failing request timestamps.

ivana: we'll run a sweep for TTL inconsistencies across our regional DNS replicas and confirm replication lag. if we find stale records we'll force a refresh and invalidate caches.

maya: action items:
- kevin: collect traceroute + failing timestamps from customer (in progress)
- ivana: INFRA-4021 created, checking DNS replication + cert rotation logs
- steven: review worker pool CA bundles and any platform-level egress proxies that could affect cert validation
- kevin: confirm customer allowlist changes and share results

kevin: noted. will update thread when customer confirms 24h stability. :thumbsup:
